content_voiceover: This slide covers the ALFA-0701 trial, which established frontline MYLOTARG, that's gemtuzumab ozogamicin, in combination with chemotherapy. Patients were randomized 1 to 1 to induction with daunorubicin 60 milligrams per meter squared on days 1 to 3, plus cytarabine 200 milligrams per meter squared days 1 to 7, with or without MYLOTARG dosed at 3 milligrams per meter squared on days 1, 4, and 7, that's the fractionated dosing schedule. If bone marrow blasts remained above 10 percent at day 15, patients got a second induction course, and notably, patients in the MYLOTARG arm did not receive MYLOTARG during that reinduction. Responders proceeded to two consolidation cycles, each with daunorubicin and high dose cytarabine, and the MYLOTARG arm received one additional low dose of MYLOTARG, 3 milligrams per meter squared, on day 1 of each consolidation cycle. The primary efficacy endpoint was event free survival, measured from randomization to induction failure, relapse, or death from any cause.
keypoints: ALFA-0701: DNR plus AraC induction, with or without fractionated MYLOTARG
MYLOTARG dosed 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4, 7 of induction only, not reinduction
One low dose MYLOTARG added to each of two consolidation cycles
keypoint_voiceover: Remember ALFA-0701 as the fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin regimen, 3 milligrams per meter squared on days 1, 4, and 7 added to standard daunorubicin and cytarabine induction. That fractionation is what made MYLOTARG tolerable after the original single high dose formulation was pulled from the market. The drug is also added at a single low dose to each consolidation cycle, and the trial's primary endpoint, event free survival, is the outcome most often quoted for this regimen.
